records.title: Brake Pedal-to-Booster Pushrod Screw Joint Detachment (Recall 24V621 / 26V240)
records.description: The screw connection (pushrod joint) between the brake pedal input rod and the brake booster actuator rod may not have been tightened to manufacturing specification at the factory. Over time the joint can loosen and the brake pedal can partially or fully detach from the booster. Audi first issued NHTSA recall 24V621000 (Audi internal code 46P6) in August 2024, then expanded it with recall 26V240000 in April 2026 after field returns revealed additional affected vehicles. The defect spans the e-tron / Q8 e-tron family built on the MLB Evo EV platform.
records.solution: Have the vehicle inspected under the open safety recall (24V621000 / 26V240000). Dealers inspect the brake pedal-to-booster pushrod screw joint and tighten it to specification at no charge; the pedal assembly is replaced if damaged. Verify recall completion via VIN at the NHTSA or Audi recall lookup before purchase. Do not drive if the pedal feels loose, has excessive free play, or has detached.
symptoms: Brake pedal feels loose or has excessive free play
Clicking or knocking sensation from the pedal
Sudden loss of braking force
Pedal detaches from booster

records.title: DC Fast-Charging Handshake Timeout and Failure to Initiate Session
records.description: A recurring owner complaint is that the Q8 e-tron AC charges normally at home (Level 1/2) but repeatedly fails to start a DC fast-charging session at public stations. The car and charger 'handshake' for several minutes, then the session times out with no energy delivered. Contributing causes include Plug & Charge authentication failures (especially on used cars with stale subscription data), outdated charging-control software, stored DC charging fault codes, and a weak 12V battery that prevents the HV system from waking. Documented on AudiWorld, e-tronforum, and EV charging guides.
records.solution: First try owner-level steps: power-cycle the vehicle, move to a different stall/network, disable Plug & Charge in MMI and start the session with an RFID card or credit card instead of the app, and rule out a weak 12V battery. If failures persist, a dealer scan to clear stored DC charging fault codes plus a charging-control / HV system software update typically resolves it; rarely a hardware (charge controller) replacement is required. Keep charging software campaigns up to date.
symptoms: DC fast charger times out before session starts
Endless handshake with public charger
Charging error message in MMI
Plug & Charge authentication failure
AC home charging works but DC does not

records.title: Front Passenger Occupant Detection System Deactivates Airbag (Recall 24V251 / 69GU)
records.description: An electrical connection in the front passenger seat's Occupant Detection System (ODS) may loosen, causing the system to incorrectly classify the seat as empty and deactivate the front passenger frontal airbag. With the airbag deactivated, it will not deploy in a crash, increasing injury risk to a seated passenger. NHTSA campaign 24V251000 (Audi recall code 69GU) covers numerous 2023-2024 Audi models including the e-tron quattro / e-tron Sportback quattro family; owner letters were mailed May 8, 2024.
records.solution: Complete recall 24V251000 (Audi 69GU). Dealers replace the passenger seat occupant detection system control module free of charge. If the 'PASSENGER AIRBAG OFF' indicator stays lit with an adult occupant in the seat, stop relying on that seat for a passenger until repaired.
symptoms: 'Passenger airbag off' light stays on with an adult in the seat
Airbag/restraint warning light
Occupant not detected by front passenger seat

records.title: Over-Torqued Brake Pressure Line Failure and Fluid Leak (Recall 24V428)
records.description: On certain 2024 Q8 e-tron quattro and Q8 Sportback e-tron quattro vehicles, a brake line connection may have been over-tightened during manufacturing. The over-stressed fitting can crack and fail, causing a hydraulic brake fluid leak. The result is reduced braking ability, longer pedal travel, and increased stopping distance. NHTSA campaign 24V428000 was filed in June 2024 with owner letters mailed July 9, 2024.
records.solution: Address under open recall 24V428000. Dealers inspect and replace the affected brake pressure line free of charge. Check brake fluid level and watch for the brake warning lamp; if pedal travel lengthens or fluid is low, stop driving and have it towed for inspection.
symptoms: Longer brake pedal travel
Soft or sinking brake pedal
Brake warning light
Low brake fluid level
Visible brake fluid leak
Increased stopping distance

records.title: Panoramic Glass Roof Water Leak into Cabin (TSB MC-10182485-0001)
records.description: Owners of e-tron / Q8 e-tron vehicles equipped with the panoramic glass roof report water intrusion into the cabin, often pooling in the front or rear footwells after rain or a car wash. Documented root causes include clogged or pinched roof drain tubes (the front drain exits below the door hinge in the A-pillar), and stress cracks in the plastic water channel surrounding the roof where it meets steel-reinforced brackets that expand at a different rate. Audi issued a Technical Service Bulletin (referenced as MC-10182485-0001) covering four distinct failure modes. The issue is reported across English and German owner communities (e-tronforum, AudiWorld, the electrichasgoneaudi GitHub issue tracker, and motor-talk.de).
records.solution: Have the dealer diagnose per the panoramic roof TSB. Repair depends on the root cause: clear or re-route clogged/pinched drain tubes, correct a pinched-shut rear drain, or replace/reseal the cracked plastic water channel. Dry out and inspect saturated carpet/underlay to prevent mold and electrical corrosion. Audi performs the repair reactively (only after water ingress is confirmed); some owners report the factory fix failing and needing a second visit.
symptoms: Water in front or rear footwell after rain
Damp or soaked carpet
Water dripping from headliner near the roof
Musty smell
Foggy windows / interior humidity

records.title: Premature Brake Pad/Rotor Wear and Brake Vibration/Pulsation
records.description: Despite heavy regenerative braking, owners report faster-than-expected friction-brake wear and a returning brake vibration or pulsation under moderate braking, sometimes persisting even after rotors and pads have been replaced. The pattern points to poor rotor machining/installation or an underlying hardware/calibration issue rather than normal wear. Because the Q8 e-tron is heavy (~2.6 t), front brake components and the air-suspension are among the most expensive non-battery repairs on out-of-warranty cars. Low regen use (which leaves rotors to do more work) and rotor corrosion from infrequent friction-brake use can also contribute.
records.solution: Have a dealer or independent measure rotor runout/thickness variation and machine or replace rotors with correct torque and bedding-in. Verify pad hardware and caliper slides. Using a stronger regenerative-braking setting reduces friction-brake duty and corrosion. If vibration returns shortly after a full brake job, escalate for a deeper inspection of hubs/wheel bearings and calibration.
symptoms: Steering wheel or pedal vibration under braking
Brake pulsation that returns after rotor replacement
Premature pad/rotor wear
Squealing or grinding from front brakes

records.title: Rearview Camera Image Fails or Is Delayed When Shifting to Reverse (Recall 25V900 / 90TV)
records.description: A software fault can cause the rearview camera to display a blank/black screen or a delayed image when the vehicle is shifted into reverse, reducing the driver's view behind the car. The Q8 e-tron / e-tron family is part of a VW Group-wide rearview camera campaign covering 356,649 U.S. Audi vehicles across 19 models. NHTSA campaign 25V900 (Audi recall code 90TV) had VINs searchable December 23, 2025, with owner notification letters mailed January 14, 2026.
records.solution: Complete recall 25V900 (Audi 90TV) at a dealer; the camera control software is updated free of charge (often resolves the blank/delayed image). Until repaired, physically check behind the vehicle when reversing rather than relying solely on the camera. A power cycle can temporarily restore the image but does not fix the underlying software defect.
symptoms: Black or blank rearview camera screen in reverse
Delayed camera image when selecting reverse
Frozen or intermittent rear camera feed

records.title: Severe Cold-Weather Range Loss and Reduced DC Charge Speed (Cold Battery)
records.description: Owners report roughly a one-third loss of real-world range in winter, with in-town range dropping to around 62% of EPA figures during prolonged sub-freezing spells. When the high-voltage battery is very cold, the car limits DC fast-charge power (commonly 40-80 kW instead of the rated ~170 kW) to protect the cells until the pack warms. The large cabin's electric heater/heat pump also draws several kW in the first 10-15 minutes. This is normal lithium-ion physics plus thermal management, but it surprises owners who do not pre-condition the pack.
records.solution: Use route-based battery preconditioning: enter the DC fast charger as a navigation destination so the car warms the pack en route, restoring charge speed. Precondition the cabin while still plugged in at home, use seat/steering heaters over cabin heat, and rely on Level 2 home charging (40-60A) to absorb seasonal losses overnight. No repair is needed unless range/charge limits persist in mild weather, which warrants a dealer battery-health check.
symptoms: Range drops sharply in cold weather
DC charging limited to 40-80 kW when cold
High consumption (30+ kWh/100km) at highway speed in winter
Slower charging until battery warms

records.title: 12V Auxiliary Battery Excessive Drain
records.description: The 12V auxiliary battery drains if the vehicle sits for more than a few days. Multiple electronic modules fail to enter proper sleep mode, causing parasitic drain exceeding 50mA. Software-related in most cases.
records.solution: Update vehicle software to latest version via dealer. If drain persists, have dealer perform parasitic draw test to identify module staying awake. 12V battery replacement with AGM type may be needed if battery was deeply discharged.
symptoms: Dead battery after sitting 3-5 days
Vehicle won't unlock with key fob
Infotainment slow to boot
Multiple warning messages on startup

records.title: 12V Auxiliary Battery Parasitic Drain
records.description: The Q8 e-tron can experience excessive 12V auxiliary battery drain when parked for extended periods. Despite having a large HV battery, the 12V system powers control modules, security systems, and connectivity features that remain active. A software bug can prevent modules from entering sleep mode, draining the 12V battery in 3-5 days of sitting. This leaves the vehicle unable to be unlocked or started.
records.solution: Update the vehicle software to the latest version which includes revised module sleep timing. If the 12V battery has been deeply discharged multiple times, it may need replacement as lead-acid batteries are damaged by deep discharge cycles. Connect a 12V trickle charger if the vehicle will sit for more than a week.
symptoms: Vehicle will not unlock with key fob after sitting 3-5 days
Dashboard shows 12V battery warning on startup
Multiple module fault codes after jump-starting
Connected services (myAudi app) show vehicle offline
Clock resets to incorrect time

communityRecommendations.content: Keep a CTEK MXS 5.0 12V trickle charger connected when parking for extended periods. It maintains the 12V battery without overcharging. The CTEK is the most recommended charger on e-tron forums.
Schedule a software update at the dealer — the latest firmware fixes the module sleep bug. You can also check for OTA updates via the MMI system under Settings > Software Update.
If the 12V battery dies, use the emergency key blade (inside the key fob) to manually unlock the driver door. The 12V battery access point is in the front trunk (frunk) area.

records.title: Charge Port Door Actuator and Locking Mechanism Failure
records.description: The motorized charge port door and its locking mechanism can fail, preventing the charge port from opening or properly latching a charging cable. The electric actuator motor or the latch solenoid can fail in cold weather or after repeated use. Some owners report the charge cable becoming locked in the port and unable to be released after a charging session.
records.solution: Replace the charge port door actuator and/or latch mechanism. In an emergency, there is a manual cable release in the cargo area to free a stuck charging cable. The actuator replacement is a straightforward repair that can be done by an independent shop if comfortable with the charge port housing.
symptoms: Charge port door will not open when pressed
Charging cable locked in port and cannot be removed
Charge port door opens but will not stay closed
Clicking noise from charge port without door movement
App shows charge port error when attempting remote open

communityRecommendations.content: If the charging cable is stuck, look for the emergency release cable in the right side of the cargo area (behind the trim panel). Pull it to mechanically release the cable lock.
In cold weather, spray silicone lubricant on the charge port door hinge and latch monthly. Ice buildup is the #1 cause of actuator strain and premature failure.
Do not force the charge port door open — the actuator gear teeth strip easily. Use the myAudi app or the button inside the car to open it. If neither works, use the emergency release.

records.title: High-Voltage HVAC Compressor Noise and Failure
records.description: The Q8 e-tron high-voltage electric HVAC compressor can develop bearing noise and eventually fail. The compressor runs on the 400V system and is responsible for both cabin cooling and battery thermal management. When it fails, the battery thermal management system cannot maintain optimal temperature, triggering reduced power and charging speed limits.
records.solution: Replace the high-voltage HVAC compressor assembly. This is a dealer-only repair due to the 400V high-voltage system. The repair requires de-energizing the HV system, replacing the compressor, evacuating and recharging the R-1234yf refrigerant system, and recalibrating the thermal management controller.
symptoms: Grinding or whining noise from front of vehicle
Battery thermal management warning on dashboard
Reduced charging speed at DC fast chargers
Reduced power/performance warning in hot weather
AC blowing warm air intermittently

communityRecommendations.content: Do NOT attempt this repair yourself. The 400V high-voltage system can be lethal. Only Audi-certified EV technicians should work on HV components. This is covered under the 8-year/100,000-mile battery/EV component warranty.

If you notice reduced DC fast charging speeds (especially in warm weather), have the HVAC compressor checked before the bearing failure becomes catastrophic. Early detection prevents cascading thermal damage to the battery pack.
Check your Audi warranty coverage — the HV HVAC compressor is typically covered under the 8-year/100,000-mile EV drivetrain warranty, not the standard 4-year/50,000-mile warranty.
